questions.question: Anthropic reported multi-agent systems used about 15 times the tokens of a chat. What does that tell you about your own task?
options: Little on its own: you need your task's bill per pattern and your measured success rates
questions.explanation: Decisions need your numbers, not averages.

questions.question: Without caching, why did the single agent read more input than the orchestrator?
options: It had a longer system prompt
Each call re-read every earlier search result in its growing context
questions.explanation: Workers never re-read each other's results.

questions.question: With prompt caching, the single agent became the cheapest. Why?
options: Its growing context is one long reusable prefix, which caching discounts heavily
questions.explanation: Many short contexts have less to reuse.

questions.question: Parallel workers cut latency only from 51 s to 43 s. Why not by two thirds?
options: Planning and synthesis still run in sequence on the critical path
questions.explanation: Latency is the sum over stages, not over calls.

questions.question: A pattern raises success from 70% to 85% and costs $0.022 more per task. When does it pay?
options: When a successful task is worth more than about $0.022 / 0.15 = $0.147
questions.explanation: V > extra cost / extra success rate.

questions.question: Most of the workers' coordination tokens were the system prompt re-read on every call. What's the cheapest fix?
options: Trim shared instructions and cache them
questions.explanation: It's saved on every call by every agent.
